content: Do you have numbers for this? Sounds like something we should have in mind

author: tomaj2
content:
Signatures in calldata are used mostly for permits, right?
From what I understand, frames txs would allow having multiple signatures declared outside calldata, and over any hash, not only the tx hash. Contracts could use that as a cheaper alternative to calldata. I'd think this would cover most uses?

author: potuz
content: Yeah I can get you numbers after tomorrow, but <@363800010518822915> has looked at this on arbitrum. If frames gives a way to send signatures away from calldata in a way that contracts can access them from an aggregate Stark at the block level (even if it's just for a single enshrined signature scheme) we should do this, it will greatly affect the fork IMO. Cc <@543900561460822016> we should look into this. It will require contract arquitectura rewiring but they'll need to do this anyway

author: terencechain
content:
I dont have a dedicated node so I only sampled blocks over 24 hours, I checked for matching signature bytes in top-level calldata to `ecrecover` calls in execution traces and found ~13% on mainnet and ~21% on arbitrum has at least 1 calldata signature. Thats likely the floor though, it could be more, I didnt check other cases like passkey signature via `P256VERIFY` since that doesnt go thorugh `ecrecover`

My understand of 8288 is it does enable contract to access the stark at the block level via some `DEP_VERIFY_FRAME_MODE`. But this will be a major change across defi stack though. (wallet -> router -> solver/relayer -> venue) all need to support that
https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8288#transaction-execution-visibility
